recommended_use: Native interacting temporal transfer and Dirichlet-form theory from the admitted finite-parent law, not a new microscopic premise or automatic physical quantization.
reading_scope_rule: Selected theorem statements, assumptions and stated derivations were inspected. This is not full-paper peer review or formal verification.
cache_rule: Cache SHA-256 binds Firecrawl extracted PDF text or the explicitly named browser DOM capture, not original PDF bytes. The ignored cache is not redistributed and can be absent from a clean checkout.

sources.title: Convergence of spectral structures: a functional analytic theory and its applications to spectral geometry
sources.version: Publisher PDF, Communications in Analysis and Geometry 11(4), 599-673; no arXiv revision asserted
sources.applicability: Abstract framework for a native FIN operator/semigroup limit.
sources.assumption_gap: Pay identification maps, Mosco lower and recovery bounds; spectral counting needs compact convergence.
sources.must_not_conclude: A path CLT alone proves spectral convergence or spatial geometry.

sources.title: From classical to quantum dynamics at Rokhsar-Kivelson points
sources.version: arXiv:cond-mat/0311345v1 identified in acquired search metadata; publication metadata separately reports 2004
sources.applicability: Generic reversible FIN similarity transform and Euclidean correlation identity.
sources.assumption_gap: Physical real-time dynamics and noncommuting instruments are not selected by the transform.
sources.must_not_conclude: Square-root stationary amplitudes derive laboratory quantum probabilities or a physical quantum clock.

sources.title: Mosco convergence of gradient forms with non-convex interaction potential
sources.version: arXiv:2105.05140v2, 24 June 2024, identified in acquired archive search metadata

sources.assumption_gap: The paper treats gradient forms with density/disintegration controls; FIN has discrete jump forms requiring a separate comparison.
sources.must_not_conclude: Non-convexity alone licenses applying the theorem to FIN.

sources.title: The Sheaf-Theoretic Structure of Non-Locality and Contextuality
sources.version: arXiv:1102.0264v7, 29 November 2011, visible in extracted archive header
sources.applicability: Exact test of compatible passive FIN readouts represented on one common probability space.
sources.assumption_gap: Specify operationally identical measurements and compatible contexts before testing extensions.
sources.must_not_conclude: A Hilbert representation or classical memory alone provides contextuality.

sources.title: Contextuality for preparations, transformations and unsharp measurements

sources.assumption_gap: Operational equivalence and convex structure must be supplied; restricted classical access does not automatically prove universal noncontextuality.
sources.must_not_conclude: Classical ontic variables or disturbance settle every generalized-contextuality question.

sources.title: Extension technique for complete Bernstein functions of the Laplace operator

sources.assumption_gap: FIN must be a complete Bernstein function of the stated base operator; positivity alone is insufficient.
sources.must_not_conclude: The extension derives physical space or applies to arbitrary positive matrices.

sources.assumption_gap: A supplied Euclidean base Laplacian, function class, normalization and weighted extension are required.
sources.must_not_conclude: Fractional asymptotics alone derive geometry, dimension or relativistic dynamics.
